title: Trajectory deck: signal and behavior stories — Q2 working draft
content:
Purpose
To provide a concise working artifact that ties Q2 OKR drafts to an executable all-hands narrative and the short list of exec update lines. This is intentionally compact so eng and GTM leads can iterate in comments — not a finished deck.

Summary / northbound signal
- Problem: teams are shipping disparate performance/latency stories; execs need a single, testable set of commitments to align resource allocation (Dedicated capacity, Private launch cadence, Console rollouts).
- Proposed single-sentence commitment for Q2: "Reduce median hosted-token cost by 18% while holding product-facing P95 latency ≤ 220ms across top-10 routes; enable Dedicated capacity GA for three enterprise customers with SLA tests."

Draft OKRs (working — measurable suggestions included)
O1: Make inference economics predictable for customers
KR1.1: Decrease median cost-per-1M tokens (hosted) by 18% vs baseline (Jan 2026) — owners: infra + optimize
KR1.2: Ship auto-batching suggestions in Optimize v0.3 and surface savings in Console for top-20 customers — owner: optimize
KR1.3: Deliver quantization recommendation engine with model-level cost delta estimates in catalog — owner: applied-ml

O2: Improve application-level latency & reliability for PLG workloads
KR2.1: P95 latency ≤ 220ms for top-10 PLG routes in hosted (measured on week-over-week synthetic tests) — owner: serving-runtime
KR2.2: Reduce dropped-stream rate during tail load by 60% (tracked via observability errors) — owner: observability + sre
KR2.3: Validate automatic fallback chain for model routing in 3 regions (canary → fallback) with documented runbook — owner: platform-engineering

O3: Accelerate enterprise adoption of Dedicated & Private
KR3.1: Onboard 3 paid Dedicated customers at committed baseline throughput ≥ 500 tokens/sec each — owner: sales + dedicated
KR3.2: Deliver Private (VPC) install doc and automated smoke tests; pass security review for first customer — owner: private-deployments + security
KR3.3: Publish SLO/SLA page and make commitment public for Dedicated — owner: product + legal

All-hands run of show (45 minutes + 15 Q&A) — draft script
- 0–5m: CEO 1-sentence frame (Katherine): where we are vs plan, single Q2 commitment (see summary)
- 5–12m: Product lead demo: cost/latency dashboard + one case study (PLG route speedup)
- 12–22m: Eng: three short signal cards (Serving runtime optimizations, Optimize suggestions, Dedicated capacity status) — each 3 minutes + 1 slide
- 22–30m: Customer story (pre-recorded) showing Dedicated onboarding friction reduced
- 30–38m: People ops & hiring snapshot (key roles we need to hit the KR cadence) + asks to managers
- 38–45m: Tactical calls to action (team-level commitments + follow-up syncs), then live poll
- 45–60m: Open Q&A moderated by Head of Product Ops

Exec update bullets (30–60 seconds each)
- Economics: Preliminary simulation shows ~14% median token cost reduction from combined batching + quantization experiments; ramp plan to 18% requires shipping Optimize UI + catalog recommendations (ETA end of April).
- Reliability: P95 trend improved 10% on synthetic tests after kernel selection changes; tail behavior still fragile under synthetic burst — SRE remediation plan in PLAT-1293.
- Enterprise: Two Dedicated pilots in progress; one customer passed security questionnaire and expects pilot contract by mid-May.

Top risks & mitigations
- Risk: Rolling quantization recommendations causes small regressions in output quality for sensitive prompts. Mitigation: Gate via evaluation harness + rollback policy; add quality regression alerts tied to prompt set (QA owner: applied-ml).
- Risk: Hiring drag delays runtime optimizations. Mitigation: Prioritize cross-team pairing, reuse kernels from partner repo, and apply short-term contract for critical SRE work.
- Risk: All-hands narrative overloads teams with tactical asks. Mitigation: Use one-pager + team commitment template; capture CTAs into a decision backlog and route to owners within 48 hours.

Decisions needed before final deck (owners and deadlines)
1) Approve single-sentence Q2 commitment (owner: exec team) — decision required by 2026-02-22
2) Lock the three top-level KR targets (cost %, latency threshold, Dedicated customer count) — product + eng — 2026-02-24
3) Confirm customer story and recording logistics (CS + comms) — 2026-02-25

Appendix: metric baselines (quick snapshot)
- Median hosted token cost (Jan 2026): $0.98 per 1k tokens (internal metric WIP)
- P95 latency (Jan 2026) across top-10 routes: 245ms
- Drop/stream error rate baseline: 0.8% during synthetic tail bursts

Appendix: owner table (copyable for comms)
- Serving runtime: Samir Banerjee
- Optimize: Aisha Patel
- Applied ML (recommendations): Lin Zhou
- Observability & SRE: Miguel Alvarez
- Dedicated & Private: Rachel Kim (solutions eng)

Notes to editors / open questions (fragments)
- Should we separate the all-hands into two shorter sessions (announce + deep-dive follow-up)? Pros: less cognitive load, more targeted technical deep dives. Cons: more scheduling friction.
- How tight should the cost target be in public comms? Suggest show target range (15–20%) until we have end-to-end telemetry from Optimize + catalog.
- Quick action item: product-ops to create team commitment template (one pager) and a Slack thread pattern for acceptance confirmations.

Unresolved items tracked as quick backlog (PLAT-1293 / INF-4821)
- Final A/B criteria for quantization enablement on hosted (who owns the guard rails?)
- SLO wording for Dedicated SLA (legal + product)
- Demo dataset for all-hands: pick 2 PLG routes that are representative and non-fatal for customers when experimenting.

If you're editing this doc: leave inline comments for any KR changes, and avoid reorganizing the top-level signal sentence without tagging execs for sign-off.
